title: Security and Compliance Concepts

header.html: Concepts of security, compliance, and identity (10–15%)
Describe the shared responsibility model; Describe defense-in-depth; Describe the Zero Trust model; Describe encryption and hashing; Describe Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) concepts
the official SC-900 study guide, skills measured as of October 21, 2026

html:
1The shared responsibility model

In the cloud, security is shared between the cloud provider and the customer. What is shared depends on the service type.

Layer On-premises IaaS PaaS SaaS
Information and data You You You You
Devices You You You You
Accounts and identities You You You You
Identity and directory infrastructure You You Shared Shared
Applications You You Shared Provider
Network controls You You Shared Provider
Operating system You You Provider Provider
Physical hosts, network, datacenter You Provider Provider Provider

Exam tip

. Data, devices and accounts and identities are always yours, in every model. The physical datacenter is always the provider's (except on-premises). The more managed the service (IaaS to PaaS to SaaS), the more the provider handles.

2Defense in depth

Defense in depth uses layers of protection, so if one layer fails the next still protects the data.

Layer (outer to inner) Protects Examples
Physical security Buildings and hardware Locks, badges, cameras
Identity and access Who signs in and what they can do MFA, Conditional Access
Perimeter The network edge DDoS protection, firewalls
Network Traffic between systems Segmentation, network security groups
Compute Servers and VMs Patching, endpoint protection
Application App code and APIs Secure development, WAF
Data The information itself Encryption, labels, access control

The data is at the center and each layer wraps around it.

3The Zero Trust model

Zero Trust does not trust anything by default, even inside the corporate network. The slogan is "never trust, always verify."

Principle Meaning
Verify explicitly Always authenticate and authorize using all available data: identity, location, device health, service, data classification, anomalies
Use least-privilege access Limit access with just-in-time and just-enough access and risk-based policies
Assume breach Segment access, encrypt data, use analytics to detect threats and improve defenses

Zero Trust protects six areas, often drawn as pillars: identities, endpoints, applications, data, infrastructure and network.

Exam tip

. The three principles are verify explicitly, least privilege, assume breach. The old model trusted everything inside the network perimeter; Zero Trust replaces it because users, devices and data are everywhere.

4Encryption and hashing

Encryption Hashing
Purpose Confidentiality: keep data secret Integrity: show data was not changed
Reversible? Yes, with the key No, one way
Output Ciphertext A fixed-length hash
Example Disk encryption, HTTPS Password storage, file checks

Types of encryption

Type Keys Use
Symmetric One shared key to encrypt and decrypt Fast, for bulk data
Asymmetric Public key and private key Key exchange, digital signatures

Where encryption is used: at rest (stored data: disks, databases) and in transit (moving data: HTTPS, VPN). A digital signature is a hash signed with a private key.

Exam tip

. Encryption can be reversed; hashing cannot. A hash proves integrity, not secrecy. Asymmetric uses two keys; symmetric uses one.

5Governance, risk and compliance (GRC)

Part Meaning Example
Governance The rules, roles and oversight that guide how security is managed Security policies, who approves changes
Risk Identifying and managing threats and their impact Risk assessments, treating risks
Compliance Following laws, regulations and standards GDPR, HIPAA, ISO 27001

GRC ties together what you must do (compliance), what could go wrong (risk) and how the organization directs it (governance).

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors uses a SaaS email service. Which responsibility stays with Fabrikam?

  • AThe physical datacenter
  • BIts data and who has access to it
  • CThe operating system of the servers
  • DThe network cables
Show the answer

Answer: B. Data, devices and identities are the customer's responsibility in every service type.

S2A company layers a firewall, MFA, encryption and a locked server room so that one failure does not expose data. Which approach is this?

  • AA single perimeter
  • BFederation
  • CDefense in depth
  • DHashing
Show the answer

Answer: C. Using several layers of protection is defense in depth.

S3An access policy checks the user, the device health and the location before every request. Which Zero Trust principle is this?

  • AAssume breach
  • BVerify explicitly
  • CTrust the network
  • DUse a shared key
Show the answer

Answer: B. Using all available signals for every request is verifying explicitly.

S4Which statement is true about hashing?

  • AIt can be reversed with a key held by the owner of the data
  • BIt keeps data secret by scrambling it for authorized readers
  • CIt is one way and shows whether data changed
  • DIt needs a public and a private key to check the result
Show the answer

Answer: C. A hash is a one-way fingerprint used to check integrity.

S5Which type of encryption uses a public key and a private key?

  • ASymmetric
  • BHashing
  • CObfuscation
  • DAsymmetric
Show the answer

Answer: D. Asymmetric encryption uses a key pair.

S6A company writes security policies, assigns oversight roles and reviews risks. Which concept covers this?

  • ASIEM
  • BXDR
  • CGRC
  • DSSO
Show the answer

Answer: C. Governance, risk and compliance organize how security is directed, assessed and regulated.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Which three things are always the customer's responsibility?

Show the answer

Data, devices, and accounts and identities.

R2What is defense in depth?

Show the answer

Using multiple layers of protection.

R3Name the three Zero Trust principles.

Show the answer

Verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, assume breach.

R4What is the difference between encryption and hashing?

Show the answer

Encryption is reversible and gives confidentiality; hashing is one way and shows integrity.

R5Symmetric or asymmetric: which uses one key?

Show the answer

Symmetric.

R6What does GRC stand for?

Show the answer

Governance, risk and compliance.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Shared responsibility data, devices, identities always yours; physical layer always the provider's; the rest shifts toward the provider
Defense in depth physical, identity, perimeter, network, compute, application, data
Zero Trust verify explicitly, least privilege, assume breach; six areas
Encryption vs hashing reversible confidentiality vs one-way integrity; symmetric one key, asymmetric two
GRC governance (rules), risk (threats), compliance (laws and standards)
